_meta.indication: Indicated to decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia; not indicated for peripheral blood progenitor cell mobilization for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, non-inferiority, multicenter trial comparing eflapegrastim (Rolvedon) 13.2 mg vs pegfilgrastim 6 mg given SC on Day 2 of each 21-day cycle
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with early-stage breast cancer receiving docetaxel and cyclophosphamide (TC) chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1
pivotal_trials.result: Difference in mean DSN (eflapegrastim vs pegfilgrastim) was -0.148 days (95% CI: -0.265, -0.033); non-inferiority demonstrated (upper bound of 95% CI <0.62 days)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled, non-inferiority, multicenter trial vs pegfilgrastim in early-stage breast cancer patients receiving TC
pivotal_trials.population: Early-stage breast cancer patients receiving docetaxel and cyclophosphamide (TC) chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1
pivotal_trials.result: Difference in mean DSN (eflapegrastim vs pegfilgrastim) was -0.073 days (95% CI: -0.292, 0.129); non-inferiority demonstrated (upper bound of 95% CI <0.62 days)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) in Rolvedon-treated patients are fatigue (58%), nausea (52%), diarrhea (40%), bone pain (38%), headache (29%), pyrexia (28%), anemia (25%), rash (25%), myalgia (22%), arthralgia (21%), and back pain (20%); serious risks include splenic rupture, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and serious allergic reactions/anaphylaxis
target_moa: Recombinant human granulocyte growth factor (G-CSF) that binds to G-CSF receptors on myeloid progenitor cells and neutrophils, triggering signaling pathways controlling cell differentiation, proliferation, migration and survival; a long-acting G-CSF analog conjugated to an IgG4 Fc via a PEG linker
modality: Other (long-acting recombinant human G-CSF analog / Fc-fusion conjugate)

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented to an Advisory Committee or any other external consultants.

summary.text: Standard-review original BLA under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act received October 24, 2019; a Complete Response letter was issued August 3, 2021 for product quality issues (no clinical deficiencies), and the drug was approved on September 9, 2022 following resubmission, based on two randomized, open-label, non-inferiority phase 3 trials

citations.quote: results of the pivotal studies that resulted in approval of G-CSFs and approved per 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act (Neupogen, Neulasta and Granix). (All other approved G-CSF products are biosimilars approved under section 351(k) of the Public Health Service Act).

The original BLA was submitted on October 24, 2019. A Complete Response letter (CRL) was issued on August 3, 2021, due to product quality issues. No clinical deficiencies were identified (see review clinical review dated June 24, 2020). The Sponsor submitted a response to the CRL on March 11, 2022.
The corrected action letter incorporates the correction of the errors. The effective action date will remain September 9, 2022, the date of the original letter.
